name: Imperial Authority
description: How strongly Ferdinand can act as emperor and enforce settlement across the Empire.

name: Confessional Legitimacy
description: Catholic confidence that Ferdinand is defending the faith and restoring order.

name: Estate Trust
description: How much imperial and territorial estates believe their liberties and legal standing remain safe.

name: Fiscal Capacity
description: The crown's ability to pay, borrow, reward allies, and keep armies functioning.

name: Military Dependence
description: Reliance on Bavaria, the League, Spain, and military entrepreneurs to solve force problems.

name: Foreign Intervention Risk
description: How likely outside powers are to see imperial policy as a reason to intervene.

name: Dynastic Security
description: The security of Habsburg rule in hereditary lands and the imperial succession.

name: Devastation
description: The social and material damage caused by armies, confiscation, quartering, and prolonged war.

name: Imperial Standing
description: Whether imperial law and opinion treat him as a wronged elector or a rebel.

name: Protestant Champion
description: Confidence of the Calvinist and Union cause that he is its defender.

name: Estate Backing
description: Support of the Bohemian estates and the German princes whose consent he needs.

name: Treasury
description: Money to pay armies and sustain a court and a cause.

name: Borrowed Swords
description: Reliance on the Union, foreign mercenaries, and freebooting captains who are not his.

name: Foreign Hands on His Fate
description: How far great powers decide his cause rather than himself.

name: Palatinate and Dignity
description: The security of his hereditary lands and the electoral title he gambled.

name: Devastation
description: The ruin his gamble brings on the Palatinate and Bohemia.
